contract: priority(vector, n, w) -> finite float. The pinned MCTS-AHD solver greedily constructs a symmetric constant-weight admissible set of ternary vectors at n=15, w=10. Score: expanded set cardinality. This is not the prime-residue admissible-tuple problem.
notes: MCTS-AHD Appendix B.1 Eq. (10) defines constant-weight ternary admissible sets. The original training solver uses n=15, w=10 and a symmetry-restricted greedy construction; the local adapter evaluates that single training instance, not the four-size validation profile or a complete MCTS search.

The upstream construction code and recovered priority baseline retain their pinned source credits. The local adapter checks finite score and actual candidate calls but does not independently certify the expanded set; validity remains unknown.
